utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to you as well, Mr. Al-Alfi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to deal with a minor procedural issue, if you would apologise us. The Chamber is informed, Mr. Kuzmanovic, that Mr. Markac, for reasons known to the Chamber by now, will waive his right to be present tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and hopefully it won't take the full time; but if necessary, he will try to be here before the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the Chamber, of course, is considering the Court schedule of this week, and sees that there's a risk that the next witness might be endangered to the extent that we might not finish and therefor is exploring, at this moment, the possibility to sit on Thursday afternoon. And if need be, that for that purpose, the Chamber would like to be more fully informed about the times needed for the next witness, next witness scheduled for two hours in chief. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. Although my understanding is that the examination will last probably closer to an hour and a half than two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, of course the Chamber has no indication yet as to how much time the next witness would take and it depends on that information what further to explore. So the Chamber would like to receive further information and at this moment is working on Thursday afternoon and, again, if need be, Friday afternoon as well. Especially Friday afternoon, I can imagine that that causes problems. If there are any problems as far as Defence teams are concerned, of course the Chamber would like to know as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as we're concerned with the following witness, we don't anticipate -- we've given a time estimate already of no more than roughly an hour for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: With the next witness, Your Honour, I did warn the Prosecution last week, and I said we did not want to be under pressure with witnesses being called last minute and we're unable properly to deal with our cases. What happens here is a large number of documents come in, sometimes four our five times a day, revised schedules, revised lists, and somehow we have to try and track this and see whether a witness is going to be used in a particular way or not, what documents are actually being used. This witness went from viva voce to 92 ter, and it causes great difficulty in trying to administer properly and assemble our materials in what is essentially a documents case to a large extent. To be frank, for the next witness I haven't really had a chance to read -- I know he has made a third statement in November of this year, and I have been briefed about that, but I haven't had a chance to read it and catch up myself with the developments with this witness from his first two statements and I have been told things have suddenly changed. And being put under pressure in those circumstances to make decisions on how properly to deal with it, in our submission, is unfair to us because we've come a long way in a very short period of having had preparations for trial on this case, and some of these witnesses I am reading for the first time in the week before they're called or a few days before they're called and having to make preparations accordingly. So, in my submission, having warned the Prosecution about this last week that there would be a difficulty with that witness, I appreciate then that he was a viva voce witness, but I did warn them that there would be a number of issues that had to be covered. I'm concerned if we are unable to properly prepare and develop our defences with the witnesses whose evidence is changing by the month. This --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber is not following closely these developments. If it reaches a point where you say, We can't do it, then of course you have to address the Chamber on the matter, as you did now, but in rather general terms. So as soon as have you made the progress needed to give us an indication, then we'd like to hear from you. I mean, just the information that you warned the Prosecution and that it is problematic, of course, is -- it's good for to us know. At the same time doesn't give a lot of assistance in scheduling for the rest of the week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: To be frank, I still haven't caught up with the third statement that's been a recent development and I'm told changes what he said previously, and I'll have to turn my attention to that this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then we'd like to hear from you as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will advise you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the same here with respect to the next witness. The statement came in yesterday late and I haven't even had a chance to look at yet, so I'm in the same position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it would not come as a surprise, Mr. Kehoe, if you find yourself in similar difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I might add just one other matter. Yesterday was the first time we got the exhibit list for the next witness. There had been no notification with regard to those exhibits, so I don't want to echo what my learned friends have said but I just wanted to add that further point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The information of a rather general nature and not yet finalized, the Chamber will continue to explore possibilities to find more time this week as you will understand. That being said, I think we can continue -- yes, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There's just one thing on the record that I want to correct. The statement was not given yesterday for the first time. It was disclosed in November when it was taken. As Mr. Kehoe said, yesterday it was the exhibit list that was sent. I just want to make the record clear on that. The statement was disclosed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: -- as soon as we received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. That is on the record now as well. Mr. Al-Alfi, this might not be very -- of great interest to you. What I'd like to hear you from and I'm also addressing the parties. I was informed that upon my instruction where I had failed to instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given, that this instruction was given to you orally immediately after yesterday's session. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Your colleague gave it to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. Then I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of the testimony that you will speak the truth, whole truth and nothing but the truth. Mr. Kay, are you ready to continue your examination -- cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, the next document I wanted to look was in tab 4 of your bundle and it is dated the 10th of August, 1995. And it again is a record of a meeting with General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is 65 ter 6152, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you would be looking at that in tab 4, Mr. Al-Alfi, while it is coming up on the screen because I'm going to ask you a general question which follows on from those questions I asked you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hold on for a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say on the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10th of August. Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Tab 4.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I've got it. I got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And we can see in paragraph 2 there had been a meeting with Mr. Pitkanen and General Cermak. On page 2, a list of the matters dealt with is set out. You can take it from me, Mr. Al-Alfi, that in fact, again, at this meeting there was no discussions of the crimes, looting, burning, or killings. It was specific issues concerning the UNCRO camp, displaced persons and interviewing detainees there and people in Croatian custody. So no discussion there of lootings, burnings and crimes, between you and General Cermak. You can check if you want, but I can tell you that's the fact.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report is reflecting a meeting which is a follow-up of the SRSG's meeting in Knin --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and the agreement with the Croatian government. So it was specific for a follow-up of other issues, not necessarily reflecting the overall situation in the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I totally agree. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's on your list, Mr. Hedaraly. I am aware of that. It's the one document which was not yet on the 65 ter list, but there were no objections adding it. But I think we adopted, more or less, the practice that if it has not yet been assigned a P number, because the list is not there yet and is not yet processed by the registrar, that you strike it from the list and that we now decide on admission as a D exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Whatever is convenient for the Chamber, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's the -- more or less the practice we adopted. Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- 6152 would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- that would be Exhibit D1209.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1209 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document at tab 5 is the 11th of August. Again, without going into the detail because it would take a lot of time, Mr. Al-Alfi, and you're able to flick through. Again, this is a meeting, again, about specific issues of restriction of movement, interviewing of people in the camp. At page 3 of the document, there is references there to -- as we can see on lines 3 and 4, to burning of houses, crops, killing of animals, destruction and looting, as being something that was happening, but it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, I haven't called up the 65 ter. I'm sorry, Your Honour, I have been sidelined. 65 ter 5058 [sic]. My apologies. 4058.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it appears on your list as unstricken as well, if Mr. Kay tenders it, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again this document has reference to a meeting with General Cermak. But the point is that at the meeting with General Cermak, that issue was not being discussed with him by you. Your meeting with him was about specific issues concerning the displaced persons within the camp, Mr. Al-Alfi, and your report and discussing with Mr. Cermak about people being in custody in the area. It's not discussing with him lootings, burnings and crimes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly when we go after the agreement, there is a follow-up of specific topics. And at that time, the main concern of the Croatian authorities was those people inside our camp. So when you go to any meeting, that definitely will not repeat everything. You will be going for a specific purpose, and for that reason, it was only specifically about the details on how the investigation or interviewing of those people inside the camp will be. But as you rightly mentioned, I was, at the same time, reflecting what was the situation. That's the same page you have referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: My concern is General Cermak and what was said to him, and that's what I'm examining with you because that's the importance, as he is on trial, to have a look at what was said to him by you and when. If we could admit that document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D1210.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1210 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And just so as to keep an order within this bundle at this stage, if we could go to the document that is tab 6 in your file, Mr. Al-Alfi. It is 65 ter 4757, and it's dated the 12th of August, 1995. And it concerns various meetings that were held on that day with various people in the area. At this time, the first thing we're going to look at concerns a meeting with Mr. Pasic, described as the newly appointed mayor of Knin. And you were searching for a name yesterday; do you recollect? And that is the name Pasic?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So long as it is in my report, that's the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps that refreshes your memory now.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. A couple of points here. He's described as the mayor of Knin. Did you in fact know that that was not his job and his title?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how he introduced himself to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He was something known as the government's commissioner for Knin. Was that a phrase that you heard?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through his own interpreter, I heard the word "mayor."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He had been appointed as the government's commissioner in 1993, under the laws of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That might be true, but the way he -- I heard it from his own interpreter was mayor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you appreciate that there was no such position within Croatian society as the mayor of a town?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have them in other societies as we know, and it's a phrase in common use, as you would agree?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in other sectors, and the word "mayor" was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to how he was described as the newly appointed mayor of Knin, I'm interested in this translation issue and how information was being passed to you because you said he had an interpreter. Didn't you use interpreters as well? Didn't you bring interpreters to meetings?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that we did not have interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You didn't bring anyone from the camp to interpret at meetings for you?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have any local interpreter at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So do you know who was being used then as an interpreter for Mr. Pasic, what this person was?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know him. I came to the meeting, and I saw this man, and he was the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. The command of the language, were you able to appreciate that, whether he had a good or poor command of the English language?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I be able to judge it when I don't know the language myself?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I must correct something. I'm told mayors did exist in Croatia, and that would be the case at that time. But he was the government's commissioner, not a mayor?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's your information, but my information -- he was introduced to me through the interpreter as mayor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. This was the first time that you'd met him?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know what his jobs and responsibilities were, aside from his title? So let's forget the title, what his actual jobs and responsibilities were?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know about the resources available to him, whether he had staff or an office?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that he an office in Knin, but other than that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you allow me to just go back one of the previous questions for one second. Mr. Al-Alfi, you said how could you judge upon the command of the English knowledge by this interpreter. You will certainly, with your background, have the experience that you would easily, or less easily, communicate with other persons in the English language. I mean, we see here in court, we hear in court that you have no great difficulties in expressing yourself in the English language, so I would, although not being a native English-speaking person, I would allow myself to give a judgement - don't worry, a positive judgement - about your command of the English language. You'll certainly be able to tell us whether had you any difficulties in communicating with this interpreter in the English language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I was referring to the Serbo-Croat language here. I didn't have any command, but through the interpreter I heard him saying mayor. I understood him, but I had no problem in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So your communication with him in English, whether he was translating or not what was said in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in the language of Mr. Cermak, but you had no difficulties in communicating in the English language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. I did not have any difficulty in understanding him in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But what was the title that was told to him or what was told to him, I did not have any command in the Serbo-Croat language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not just focussing on that title; I'm focussing on the conversation in its entirety. So you had no difficulties in communicating in English. And do you remember whether he was a native Croatian person, either by -- or let's say, was he from the former Yugoslavia, that interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He was. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm just going back to Mr. Pasic. Had you appreciated the task that he had to face in coming into an area where the state had had no government at all, since the creation of that state in 1991?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's only a judgement. I'm not to pass a judgement here. But I understand that he was there for the first time, that's correct. I mean, after the fall of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just going back on to the interpreters again, wasn't there a system that when there was a meeting arranged between the United Nations and any representatives of the Croatian government or institutions, that the UN would send an interpreter for those meetings?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you know that this area has -- what witnessed what it witnessed. So even if we had interpreters they would have been locals. They would have ran away. So there was no one. We were there without any local interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We've heard evidence in this court, you see, and it's right I point this out to you, that there were interpreters used who were in fact in the camp and they worked on a daily basis for the UNCIVPOL or General Forand or anyone who was having meetings with the Croatian institutions.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if there were any, then they did not work for my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could it have been the case that someone was sent along to the meeting from the UN and that you didn't appreciate that they were from the UN?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, put it this way. It's more likely that the UN would have sent interpreters along, rather than the Croatian institutions sending interpreters along for meetings at that time.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had an interpreter, I would have taken him or her with me, definitely, because that would be an UN interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There it is. There it is. But looking at Mr. Pasic, did you appreciate that whatever his job title was that he was coming into a place where he didn't have a large number of running offices and institutions working on his behalf, because for the first time the Croatian state was coming into this part of its territory where it had never had its control and authority and its institutions before. This was -- this was a first in this region. Did you appreciate that?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because you discuss whether he was effective, and you believed he was ineffective, but did you sufficiently appreciate problems that he would have been facing in providing civil institutions to enable things to run at that time in Knin?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not discuss these problems with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That wasn't the question, whether he discussed. I'm looking at your mind, if you forgive me, and whether you appreciated, whether you appreciated, whether -- because have you made a judgement about him, that he was ineffective, so I'm asking whether you appreciated -- whether he discussed it or not is another matter. Whether you appreciated.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I appreciate it if he did not discuss it with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, sometimes I can see persons having problems, where they do not express these problems to me but from other circumstances I feel or I see that they have these problems. Now, the question apparently Mr. Kay is putting to you is whether in any way, whether he told you or not you appreciated the difficulties he was facing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, the word appreciate that means I fully understand him. That's my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then did --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that's why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- did you form an opinion on the basis of what you saw and heard, whether or not directly from Mr. Cermak, what kind of problems he was facing in performing his tasks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I understood that it was only a few days, and I realized that not everything will be in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think you mentioned Mr. Cermak but the question was related to Mr. Pasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pasic. I apologise, yes. With this correction, the same -- you gained the same impression as far as Mr. Pasic is concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I apologise for the slip of the tongue. Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Not at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, at this meeting with Mr. Pasic, did you discuss in any sort of detail with him as to what the Croatian authorities were trying to achieve at this time in relation to the civilian institutions in the area?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware that on the 6th of August of 1995 that the minister of interior had been to Knin and opened for the first time the police station in Knin?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say the 6th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, we were in the camp, sir. We were not allowed to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, it was, did you know. Not where you were, but did you know, because maybe you are somewhere else but you receive information. You put other people's information in your reports, after all. It's did you know that, that on the 6th of August, for the first time, the police station opened in Knin?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that in the following two weeks further police stations opened up in the region of Knin, places like Benkovac, Donji Lapac, other places. Did you appreciate -- were you aware of that at that time?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If anyone would be aware it would be the UNCIVPOL, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware that the civilian police were bringing in policemen to man those police stations as they opened up in the area?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, if anyone would be aware, it would be the UNCIVPOL. Not me. I'm carrying the civilian, humanitarian and political side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, at this meeting -- in this report, you referred to a meeting with General Cermak - that's on page 3 of the document, paragraph 3 - I just want to put this. Again, you're not discussing looting, burnings and crimes with him. You're discussing other matters concerning you at that time, normalization of civilian life and, again, the displaced persons in the UN camp. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you notice that in this meeting I accompanied the Sector Commander, and the Sector Commander was having specific issues to discuss with General Cermak, and I said throughout my testimony that in many of the instances, I accompanied the Sector Commander to meet General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I did not raise any other issues here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was specific for a specific purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this document could be made an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D1211.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1211 is admitted into evidence. It appears on your list, Mr. Hedaraly, therefore, I did not ask for any objections. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document that I wish to produce -- excuse me, Your Honour. Exhibit D56, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a meeting on the 18th of August, Mr. Al-Alfi, and a report --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you tell me which folder it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This isn't actually in your folder. It's a court exhibit already.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In that folder you have some of your documents. Many more have gone into evidence beforehand. But if you look at the screen in front of you, you will see there our Exhibit D56, and it is a document of the 18th of August. Again, there a reference to a meeting with Mr. Pasic, and he is described there, and there's discussion of that meeting, and we can see at b, the mayor explaining the shortcomings in tackling civilian problems due to unpreparedness. If we go to, as if we have no need to look further at that - the Court have already - to page 3 is the reference to a meeting with General Cermak --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will come on your screen, Mr. Al-Alfi. It takes a while to get page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 we can see the reference to the meeting there, the initial discussion about the displaced persons. And then in the second paragraph: "During the meeting, I also brought to the attention of General Cermak our concern about the continuing reports of houses and farms set on fire in the villages and looting, and asked him about the measures taken from his side to stop such acts. General Cermak shared this concern with us and expressed his unhappiness about its continuation. He promised tough action against those who commit such acts. He also explained that some of these acts must be carried out by civilians who return to the area and seek revenge, taking advantage of the lifting of the restrictions on their movement in the area."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you read "must be carried out" where the text reads "may be carried out."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. Yeah. May be -- explained that some of these acts may be carried out. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is the first instance at your meetings of you raising the issues of crimes with him, on this date?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this date? Yes, I raised it with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 18th of August, yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not the first. But I raised it with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. This is the first time you -- you said to General Cermak and raised with him about crimes. You may have spoken to other people, and crimes were happening, but this is the first time you discussed it with him. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, if you refer to the same paragraph, at the beginning of it you can see because of the occasion --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I was also accompanied by the Human Rights Action Team. So that is the occasion to raise these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Absolutely. We're on agreement on this, as to what it is, but the question of you bringing it to his attention is an issue in the case, all right? And this is when you did, and we can see here what you reported him as saying, that he shared his concern, he was unhappy, and he promised tough action against those who commit such acts.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is in there, I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, may I nevertheless seek clarification. Earlier, and I don't know whether I fully understood you, Mr. Kay asked you whether this was the first time you raised this issue with Mr. Cermak on this date, which means that you had not raised it at an earlier date with him. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I said in my response to Mr. Kay that this was not the first time, but this was the first time that was specifically for this purpose, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I felt some ambiguity so therefore I sought this clarification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, I take it that you will then further explore the earlier occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have been through all your reports and this is the first time of your reports that you mention bringing to General Cermak's attention the issue of crimes. In your other meetings, you brought up the displaced persons, the issue over interviewing people in the camps, freedom of movement, other issues with which you were concerned, as part of your humanitarian brief. The first report by you of bringing -- of saying to him about crimes is here on the 18th of August.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was by me, as I said earlier, the meetings with General Cermak -- because it is now military dealing with military, it was General Forand dealing with General Cermak. If I had the occasion at this time, because it was the Human Rights Action Team, maybe I did not in details discuss it with General Cermak in previous meetings because that was not the occasion for that purpose. But this is not the first time I raise it with General Cermak. It was even earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: General Forand's reports are in evidence, but I'm talking about you. You were questioned by Mr. Russo yesterday, and he made a summary of your evidence to the Court and a statement about your evidence, and what I'm saying is, this was the first time that you, as an individual, raised it with General Cermak about crimes being committed.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the first time, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe the first time I reported it, reflected it clearly here, but it's not the first time I raised it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why is it not in any earlier report, if you did so?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the other reports are talking about specific issues, as I pointed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have other reports from you. They're all in evidence. And they deal with a wide variety of matters, general matters, specific matters, such as displaced persons, interviewing detainees at the camp. This, concerning crimes, is a specific matter as well, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true. But don't forget that by then the Human Rights Action Teams arrived in sector, and by then, already now we started to have specific issues to discuss on this action. Or in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that is why, on this occasion, this was the first time you discussed it.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe more details, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let me take it further this way. General Cermak was not denying those crimes were taking place, was he?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, we have now dealt with the meeting which is reported in this document, and Mr. Al-Alfi told us that he had raised the matter earlier. If you ask him from this report we see that he apparently is not denying that such crimes may have happened, but your question did not focus on this report or any of the earlier meetings where the matter, although not reported, was raised. And I would seek clarification from Mr. Al-Alfi whether at any earlier occasion when you raised the issue of crimes although we do not find it in the reports, whether he, at those earlier occasions, ever denied crimes to be committed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and if I recall correctly you will see even in one of my earlier reports whenever I went and talked to him about looting and all that, including my asking him whether about my own house was safe and he gave me the advice that you better go and take your things from your house. That means he was aware of what was going on in the area. I discussed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So at no instance he denied that this may have happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you believe he was in a position to deal with your reports about what you were saying? Did you believe he had the power and authority to deal with it by commands or orders?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not pass a judgement, but so long we were informed formally that he is the first man in the sector, then I would believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that there had been an official notification to the UN of his position. You said that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. To Zagreb, to our headquarters in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Now what document was that notification?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about it, but my headquarters informed me that he is appointed officially by the government of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your headquarters informed you?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And he was appointed officially by the government of Croatia, but as what?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact title, but he was the military governor or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know if Croatia had such an institution as military governor?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not supposed to ask all these details. All I know, who is the person with whom I would deal in the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah. Did you know he was appointed by the president as the Zborno Mjesto of Knin?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of this terminology, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The commander of the Knin garrison?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Might be true, but that's the first time I hear it. But I knew that he was the first man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know exactly what his authority was?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know exactly, but so long we were informed officially that, Anything, you deal with him, that means he had the overall authority or the top authority in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does it? If you've got anything, you deal with him. Does that mean you've got total authority in the area?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you explain exactly what's your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, if I say to you, Deal here with Mr. Mak, does that mean he has the total authority in the Defence case for Mr. Cermak?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the government of Croatia tells me that he is the man representing the government, the top official, then I have to take it as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But the government of the Croatia didn't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me. I mean tells our headquarters and headquarters informs us. That's what I mean by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You don't actually know what the government of Croatia told your headquarters. You don't know what the government of Croatia told your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was conveyed to me by my headquarters, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you know what they were told?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What exactly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it would be safe to say it was an assumption you came to.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not an assumption. It is an information I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know that General Cermak had just nine people working for him in the Knin garrison?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- I was not allowed to question how many people he had to work for him at all. Exactly he did not ask me how many people are working for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. But did you know; that was the question.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know that he couldn't command units within the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not my judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But did you know? If that is a fact, did you know that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kay, your question was what he could, and that is partially a matter of fact and partially a matter of judgement. To that extent, I think Mr. Al-Alfi responded to part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know he couldn't order troops to clean up the town for him?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know that although he gave orders for stolen UNCRO vehicles to be returned, he couldn't order the troops, the units in the Croatian army, to go and look for them?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you, as you had more dealings with Mr. Cermak, begin to get doubts about the extent of his authority?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no doubt about his authority. Question was how far he can implement it. And then later on when he disappeared from the sector without any announcement, I started to question that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know that he had just been appointed to his post on the 5th of August, and until that appointment, he had been in civilian life?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first encounter I knew General Cermak was in the sector. I did not know before that what he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. In your meetings with General Cermak, you next brought to his attention crimes that were taking place on the 24th of August, 1995. That's not in your bundle, Mr. Al-Alfi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's at Exhibit D151. And page 2, in paragraph 5 is the reference to this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The other parts of the meeting dealing with the other issues that we've already referred to. And, again, we can see the note made here of him accepting the fact of the crimes being committed, burning houses and looting. And he informed you that he had already issued strict orders to civilian and military personnel to stop such acts. Did you appreciate, or were you aware, that he had to refer those matters to others and ask them to issue orders to stop crimes or to enforce the law?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you read my report correctly, this confirms that he had the authority, because he issued -- he said that he issued these orders to others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that's what we're going to just look at.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You're basing it upon what he said to you --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Rather than what he could actually do.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Without knowing whether, despite what he said, he could only refer these matters to others to get them to enforce such orders.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take it as he said it, but if there are other internal procedures within his authority, that's not my business to ask him about the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm just going to go through a number of matters concerning General Cermak at this time. You told us already you were unaware of the resources available to him, as to what he had at his disposal, his office, the staff working for him. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah. You had no knowledge of how the Croatian military structure was organised. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How the command and control of those parts of the military structure worked.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's for our military, not for me as civilian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In your recorded interview, you assumed he had the power to give orders to units. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. Because being the first man, the governor of the area, or whatever name, title it has, otherwise, what would be -- is it a nominal head? That was -- that was my assumption, based on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You never appreciated, did you, that he was sent down to Knin with one of his tasks being to help the UN, as a specific job, to be a point of contact and help with whatever problems you had?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was sent to Knin with a different capacity. But because of being in Knin, then it was agreed with the UN that he -- we should -- he should be our contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So do you know whether or not before he got to Knin, whether he had been sent there specifically to deal with the UN as one of his jobs?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not informed about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. That he was a point of contact for the UN and was sent there to help you.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you rephrase your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sure. Were you aware that he was sent there as a point of contact to help you?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I dealt with him as the governor of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The question had been asked and answered previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry if it has but ... excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- it wasn't the first time that the same or similar question was put to the witness more than once. Mr. Kay, also in view of the time, if you have heard the answer once or twice or three times, then there's no need to put it again to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, probably lost more time now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a comment. Mr. Hedaraly raises an issue and there is some merit in it, and then you should refrain from such comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- and I extend my apologies to him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware that the other task he was sent down to Knin to perform was the normalization of life in that town, to get the town running?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware, but that's what I expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That he was sent there not with military tasks to perform. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. But how would he, under military rule, control an area if he is not -- has -- if he had no military task?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And was there military rule? Was there a law that it was military rule?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it, but that's what I expect under those circumstances at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware that he was sent to Knin at that time to help try and get businesses working, shops open, and services running?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may be the case, but I'm aware of one thing: That he was amongst the first immediately in Knin. So it's a military situation, how would I expect to talk about businesses unless this military situation first is stabilized. So you can see that it was with the military offensive. What was the details of his task, I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Ministry of Interior of the Croatian state was issuing orders for the running of the police, what they were to do, how they were to be manned, and the whole structure of the civil and police government?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that was the case, we were not informed. I mean, we in Knin were not informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you appreciate that General Cermak was just being put before you as a front man, to be the man you went to?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not tell me that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you appreciate the fact that most, if not all, of General Cermak's tasks were nothing to do with the military at all?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's a correct statement, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you disagree?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah. In your interview with the investigators of the Prosecution, you stated about what you would expect he would have at his disposal - staff, headquarters, military personnel - do you remember that when you stated that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: To the extent we're going to refer to his interview, can we get a specific reference to it so that both us and the witness can refer to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm summarizing it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could approximately give the pages, where to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, if we go to page 84 of Exhibit P1160.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is that my testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, it is --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I gave to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It becomes your testimony.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it's the passage where you give your view about the Croatian army, disciplined army, chain of command has to be followed. And I'm sure he was informed of every small bit that happened in his area of responsibility. There's that passage there. Here we are, at page 85. Certainly he should have reports and briefings from his commanders. And without having to read the full 110 pages, there's another passage which I can't put my finger on. But we know that we can see the picture, that he would have briefings from commanders, that was in your mind --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I -- can I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you would see here the word "commanders" is with small C. I meant subordinates, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are trying to tell me that he had his own commanders higher than him. But here commanders, that means the commanders in the areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's what I mean as well, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is what I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's good that it is clarified, but I did not understand the question of Mr. Kay to refer to any higher up commander but just those in command in the area which would report to Mr. Al-Alfi -- to -- not you, Mr. Al-Alfi, to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Cermak, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Don't think what I -- I totally agree with you. That's the impression. I'm not saying anything else other?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- than what you've said here. And -- because that's what I'm dealing with.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The subordinates, the commanders underneath him. And in one of your reports you refer to meeting Major Gojevic, who you described as the deputy military governor. Did it occur to you that the deputy military governor, that gap in rank from major to three- or four-star Colonel General, that there was a hierarchy missing of command? Did it occur to that you that was unusual?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the area -- the period where General Cermak was mostly out of the area and trying to negotiate about the number of those to be handed over who were in our camp to the Croatian authorities. This man -- and if you noticed in some of my reports, I even questioned and I even called him, like, a liaison officer, to receive and to say I will come back to you. I agree with you that the gap was big from, say, a two-star general to a major.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And you expected because of what you believed -- and I'm not doubting your belief. Understand that, Mr. Al-Alfi. I'm not saying you're coming here, giving us something that's not your belief, and I've made it clear in my questions that it is your belief and that you hold that. What you expected was that he would be in command of the military units in the area. That is right?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That he would be able to issue orders to those units and that they would have a responsibility to follow them?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I took issues with him, he did not say, I have no command over these military. He said, Yes, I will deal with it, and sometimes he even was talking to his subordinates in their local language, like giving immediate instructions what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Without you knowing exactly what their --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- jobs were?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Even -- exactly?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And you would have expected him to be able to be briefed by the local -- by the Military District on what was happening?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I expected -- that's the normal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You would have expected that he would know where the troops were in the region?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where they were barracked?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly -- if you are in charge, you have to know everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Where -- how to communicate with them?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know how he would communicate with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you would expect it if he was the commander, that he would know if his order was issued this way, that it goes through the chain to end up with this unit in Benkovac or wherever. That's what you were expecting?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I expected that, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That the activities of those units and soldiers would be reported through a chain to him. You expected that?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That what the units were to do next, that he would be planning that?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. He was on the TV every day, telling all the people of Croatia what's happening every day. That means he is informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You would expect as well that those orders and commands from his subordinates that he had to be kept informed of, that were important matters, would be sent to him?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only important. Everything he should be informed of. That's what I expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the logical sequence of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that's what you believed was happening?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I believed should happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah. What you believed should happen. You believed could be happening or was happening; I don't know. Did you believe if it was happening like that?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he is a commander, that's -- have you to take it for certain that this is the normal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kay. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can start now or we can take an early break. However you wish to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could take an early break. Could I perhaps pay a little bit of attention -- it might be convenient for Mr. Al-Alfi to listen to it as well. Mr. Kay, you took considerably less time than you -- Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm just taking some instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You took considerably less time than you indicated before. Now Mr. Al-Alfi has expressed some concerns to the Victims and Witness Unit about when he could leave. Our earlier assessment was that it might take us into earlier Thursday morning, but in view of the time you took, could I hear from the other Defence teams whether they want to adapt their estimates or whether it is still what it was, which would lead us to believe that we could finish this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are a couple of smaller issues that have arisen, very small, and we're going to get a video during the break to show the witness in light of one of his answers. But I definitely anticipate that he -- at least with respect to the Gotovina Defence, he should finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Agreed, Your Honour, today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, in view of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Al-Alfi. You don't have to thank me, Mr. Al-Alfi, because it was on the mind of the Chamber that the parties would have a full opportunity to examine and to cross-examine you, but if it turns out that that will be finished today, that would meet some of your concerns, if I was well-informed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. I really appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps we take an early break now, and we resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Misetic. Mr. Misetic is counsel for Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Al-Alfi.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, I'd like to take you to the statement that you gave in 1998. And if I could draw your attention to page 23, line 28. And there in your statement you -- you're talking about the days preceding Operation Storm and you say --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say page 23?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On line 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The sentence actually starts on line 27.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But you're talking about -- and this in the context of events that are taking place prior to Operation Storm, and you say prior to that you -- "Our estimates are around 100.000 troops to mass," meaning you -- you can't find it?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I cannot find it. Which page are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have it as page 23 of the 1998 statement that you gave. And if you start -- let's look at line 26. There's a sentence there that begins: "Our estimates ..."

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. It says: "Our estimates was around 100.000 troops to mass and saying either we are allowed to put our troops, because that was their interpretation of the UN Security Council resolution, that the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Croatia which is they knew that it was impossible for the Serbs to accept it. Because it's like behind them. Now, I understood the sentence that what you were saying was that it was impossible for the Serbs to accept the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Croatia. Is my interpretation correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpretation is to accept that they put the troops, because see the sentence itself where it put the troops behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So that it was impossible for them to accept --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Putting the troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I see. Okay. Very good. If we could turn to page 26, and this is your description of the morning of the 4th. And you say, beginning at line 29: "No. Everything was asleep, dead and normal. The only cars may be moving in that time was the UN cars. It was a declared curfew. So it's not undeclared. It is a declared curfew. For the local residents, they cannot be until 6.00." Can you explain a little bit more about what was happening there in terms of the curfew?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time the area was still under the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they -- in preparation maybe of what is going on because the atmosphere was preparation for war, they declared officially on the radio that it is curfew for the locals from that time. Since that time. But they cannot impose that curfew on the UN. That's why I said the only cars moving that night were the UN cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So as a result of that curfew, there were no civilians on the streets? Was that what you saw on the 4th?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That was before the operation itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. How did you come to know that there was curfew in place?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, it was announced on the local radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The RSK radio, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you know how long the curfew regime had been in place?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As -- well, I'm not sure, but it was few days before the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether the Croatian army would have known that at 5.00 a.m. there wouldn't be civilians outside as a result of the curfew regime?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I do believe that they must have been monitoring the radio of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, if you would allow me. You said it was broadcast on the radio. Could you hear that directly or was it translated to you by anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was translated to us, sir, because this is before the operation itself. So we had interpreters --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You still had interpreters --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you a little bit about the next -- sorry, on page 29 of your statement, and I will be jumping around a little bit so we won't go in --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- in sequential order.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You discuss at page 29, going on to page 30, that you were invited to a meeting in the afternoon -- I believe it's of the 4th, where it was discussed --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was of the 5th. The first day of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, if you take it from me that all parties in this case agree that the first day of the operation was the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- I meant the first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So on the 4th of August, you went with General Forand to this meeting with the ARSK in the afternoon of the 4th?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you were present when conversations were held with representatives of the RSK about an evacuation that was to take place?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we turn to page 31. And you discuss -- I'm sorry. I'm sorry, if we could go to page 30. I apologise. In your statement you discuss what was discussed at that meeting. And if you look at line 18 --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- you say: "They were shaking and they started demanding that they want -- if I'm not mistaken, 70.000 litres of oil for cars and they wanted 500 trucks to transport the civilians, because they were fighting as usual, and they would continue fighting. But the civilians are getting injured," and so you want to move them. Now, if we go to page 31. And at line 26, I believe you write, after the meeting. You say: "We told our headquarters this is their demand. We can't, we can't provide vehicles, but if it means that civilians are to be saved, the headquarters gave us the approval." Who is the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our headquarters in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In Zagreb. Okay.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zagreb. Because we deal -- we have to take instructions and approval from our headquarters in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is Mr. Akashi in your headquarters in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the head of the whole mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could have, please, Exhibit D337.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, I'm going to show you a report that Mr. Akashi sent to Mr. Annan on the evening -- in the evening of the 4th, and there are time stamps here. For example, if you look in the -- off in the right-hand corner you can see a time stamp of when this document was received, I believe in Geneva, and it says at 2002 on the 4th of August. And if we turn to the next page at paragraph 4 -- well, first before we turn the page, I'm sorry. You see the report and it is an update on the current situation in Croatia. A copy goes to Mr. Stoltenberg in Geneva, and I believe this may be, in fact, the copy that was sent to Mr. Stoltenberg, which is why the Geneva time stamp there.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were you reporting from Knin -- you just said that you talked to your headquarters. Were you sending written reports from Knin to Mr. Akashi in Zagreb on the 4th, or were you orally communicating this information?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not reporting but if you notice from the report itself it says UNMOs, military observers --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, forget the --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and they have their own chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's put aside the report for a second. Do you recall, on the 4th, whether you sent any written reports from Knin to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes. I mean, it was daily, sometimes more than one report a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: After your meeting with the RSK officials in the evening of late afternoon/early evening of the 4th, did you send a written report to Zagreb about what was discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please, in this document. Now, if you look at paragraph 4, Mr. Akashi writes to Mr. Annan and says: "We have been advised by the civil affairs office in Sector South that the Knin leadership have requested UNHCR and UNPF assistance in evacuating approximately 32.000 civilians from Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac, and Knin, to Petrovac, and Banja Luka in Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now the reference to the civil affairs office in Sector South, that would be you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. That would -- now what I just read, that was information that you had sent to Mr. Akashi on the -- in the evening of the 4th of August. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if you notice from the report, not necessarily all of it, because from the report it mentions a number of areas and Knin. That means it can be also from Sector North which was not under my control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. But all of those towns are in Sector South?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying, no, because we had two sectors. If they are in Sector South, then it can be from the military, because here we are talking about military and we have inform. But if that is there, I don't recall exactly the specific areas, but I was reporting to my headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just if we could -- I would just want to make sure that the transcript is accurate, page 42, line 8.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which? 42, line 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In front of you on the screen? No, no, on the screen. The actual transcript --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- of what you just said, at line 8. Let me ask you again, just so the record is clear. After your meeting with the RSK officials in the evening of -- or late afternoon, early evening of the 4th, did you send a written report to Zagreb about what was discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Going back to the document on the screen, in fact, at the meeting -- if you look on the screen what's reported here. What I am asking you is did you report that the Knin leadership asked for UNHCR and UNPF assistance in evacuating approximately 32.000 civilians from Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac, and Knin, to Petrovac and Banja Luka in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it exactly. But if he referred to us, definitely there was something of that sort. Because his reports also will depend so long he mentioned UNHCR, that means UNHCR because we had a representative of UNHCR. He has all reports, he receives all reports from all areas and then he puts his own reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
