utterances.text: Well, what I'm particularly interested in is the last eight words in that sentence, that first sentence. Sorry, nine words. To Petrovac and Banja Luka in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now, at the meeting that you had with the RSK officials, they told you that the evacuation was going to Petrovac and Banja Luka; correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was there any doubt in your mind when you left that meeting with the RSK officials on the evening of the 4th that their intention was to evacuate these civilians to Petrovac and Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had to take their word, what they said. That's why the arrangements were according to what they told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you recall them specifically telling that you the arrangement was to be that they are sending the civilians to Petrovac and Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the person who told you this?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember it exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember a person named Kosta Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But at that meeting there were a number of their officials, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Registrar, if I could call up Exhibit D712, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, I'm going to show you --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one are --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You don't have a copy of the document. I'm going to show you a report of a conversation on the 4th of August between Mr. Roberts, who you will recall was the press and information officer for Sector South, and a reporter that took place at 1415 on the 4th of August. And if you look at the fourth paragraph -- Obradovic is the name of the journalist. It says: "Asked by Obradovic on the situation in the town regarding the civilians, Roberts said that there was no panic among the civilians" --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you -- which one you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you look on your screen on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Four paragraphs down?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Obradovic is the name of the journalist. So it says: "Asked by Obradovic on the situation in the town regarding the civilians, Roberts said that there was no panic among the civilians; however, in his opinion, the people were extremely shocked and surprised by the shelling this morning, apartments have been destroyed and many windows and shop windows broken." Now, you were in Knin on the 4th. Do you agree that by the afternoon of the 4th, that there was no panic -- by the early afternoon of the 4th, that there was no panic in the town?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What is your position?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were no civilians to panic. I mean there were not many. And I was in the -- in my headquarters. I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So you don't know whether there was panic?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, let me then show you ... okay. I'll move on. Let's talk about the shelling. First, are you -- do you have any military experience?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Had you ever been in a situation before where you found yourself to be under artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sector West, Drvar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And when?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operation Flash.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now in terms of the assessments of the shelling that were taking -- that took place on the morning of the 4th, were you in fact relying on assessments made by UN military personnel?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Any specific individuals amongst the UN military personnel upon whose assessments were relying?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, my talk is direct with General Forand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to speak to Colonel Leslie?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, General Leslie was the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you speak to General Leslie on the 4th of August about the shelling?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in the headquarters. We talk about it all the time, and we discuss -- we were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then let me take you back to page --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because by then we were already moved even from our houses inside the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me take you back to page 27. Page 27 of the -- your statement in 1998, I'm talking about. At line 24, you begin and you say: "It was just shelling the whole town. I think if I'm not mistaken, according to the military, our military, they assessed that in the first few hours, I mean, two, three hours, it was shelling at the range of maybe more than 10.000 per hour." Do you recall who amongst your military told you that it was shelling at the rate of 10.000 per hour?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly, but as I told you, my talk is always with General Forand or Leslie, Colonel Leslie.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, 10.000 per hour and you say two -- in the first two or three hours, it was assessed to be shelling at the range of 10.000 per hour. So if we're talk two or three hours, obviously we're talking about 20 to 30.000 shells falling on Knin in the first three hours of the operation. Did you subsequently, after you were able to exit the compound, make an assessment as to whether Knin appeared to have been hit with 20 to 30.000 shells or more, given that you are just talking about the first two or three hours there.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we talk about hearing the shelling, don't forget we hear the shelling inside Knin and we can hear even in the outskirts of Knin. That's what I refer to as the number. When we went out, well, we -- as far as we were allowed to be, and from our military that they saw some damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First of all, you're talking about the outskirts of Knin. What do you define as the outskirts of the Knin?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean outskirts of the city of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right, but can you describe what you mean by out -- are you talking about other villages or are you talking about Dinara mountains?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't know where, but we can say all the area. I mean, it can be other villages outside. It can be the Dinara mountain. It can be anywhere because we don't know where they land.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you believe that because General Forand, General Leslie and yourself were subjected to the artillery fire, that you were not capable of providing an objective assessment of -- of the shelling of Knin?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not true. Because it's not personal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could I have 1D00-0741, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, I'm going to first ask you whether you've ever seen -- on the screen, if you could look, please. This is an article from the New York Times from March 21, 1999, and I'm going to ask you first based on content of the report whether you had any knowledge that this report had been published. And it says -- the title was "War crimes panel finds Croat troops cleansed the Serbs." And if I could -- you tell me if I'm wrong, and I didn't look at it very carefully, but when you gave the statement in 1998, where were you working at the time?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I was working for the UN in Morocco, MINURSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you spend any time in New York during that time-period?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I just saw the 212 area code, so I thought maybe you may have been working in New York as well.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started working in New York as such in 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at it, this is a report about what the Tribunal had concluded up to that point about Operation Storm. And if we go to page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to object so early. Usually I would go on with the questioning, but since the witness has not seen the article and now the question seems to -- if I can complete my objection, if you don't mind. Now he's asking about an internal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is -- is it an objection that can be raised in the presence of the witness or not, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He hasn't said what Mr. Hedaraly says he said he did not say he hadn't seen the article. I haven't shown it to him yet, so I don't know how he could say he doesn't know or hadn't seen it. That's why we're taking it through this process.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, then he should be first asked whether he's seen it before showing him a section of it and asking him if he's familiar with it. There -- I mean, there's a broader issue of the admissibility of this document, and I think we've had a conversation, the Prosecution with Mr. Misetic, about it. We can raise that issue now because this document is completely unrelated with this witness's evidence. And there have been other issues with newspaper articles in this case, so perhaps we can deal with that before the witness -- before the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We usually decided these matters once we had seen these documents, but I take it that -- let's give Mr. Misetic an opportunity to introduce the matter. And we'll more than ever listen with care to how he phrases his question and how he takes the witness through this document, which apparently tells us what this Tribunal's opinion is. That's -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, it -- that's not the only thing, Your Honour, and I would add that -- two points. One, that not only did the Prosecution not have a chance to interview this witness, we didn't have an opportunity to interview this witness, so I don't know what he knows or doesn't know about the subjects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, let's -- if you proceed with the required caution, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, I'm showing you the portions of the article because just by looking at a title of an article you, of course, may not know immediately what the substance of the article is. But given your involvement in this case, you may have heard something about what's contained in this article. That's why I'm putting them to you. This article talks about the conclusions reached by the Prosecutor's office in 1998 or 1999. And if you look at page -- we're on page 3, the first full sentence there says: "The most contentious recommendations of the investigators related to the shelling of Knin" --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the first one-line sentence at the top of your page there, on the screen. Do you see it? There's the carry-over -- there it is right there.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So it says: "The most contentious recommendation of the investigators related to the shelling of Knin." The next paragraph discusses testimony that had already been given by General Forand and General Leslie to the Tribunal, and you can read that. And then if we scroll down a little bit, there's a paragraph that begins: "But the report ..." "But the report goes on to quote an American lawyer at the Tribunal, Clint Williamson, as seeking to discredit the Canadian officer's testimony. They were 'not capable of detached analysis,' he said, according to the investigation report. "Mr. Williamson, who described that the shelling of Knin as 'a minor incident,' said that the Pentagon had told him that Knin was a legitimate military target." And if we scroll down, it talks about the indictment review in this case. In the paragraph it says: "Then the review panel broke for lunch." And if you go to the middle of that paragraph, it says: "The review concluded by voting not to include the shelling of Knin in any indictment. A conclusion that stunned and angered many at the Tribunal." Now, my first question to you is: Do you recall hearing something about this report when it came out in 1999?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Have you had any contact with General Leslie or General Forand since Knin?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. Just when I meet some people who know them, I just say, Say hello to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Based on the fact that they told you on the 4th of August that the shelling was occurring at the rate of 10.000 [Realtime transcript read in error "1.000"] per hour, do you think potentially that they really weren't capable of detached analysis?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That can be your assessment, but I don't know. They told me. I told you what they told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were you aware at any time that after you gave your testimony to the Tribunal in 1998, and after Generals Forand and Leslie had given their statements as well, were you aware at any time that the Prosecution had decided initially not to include the shelling of Knin in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think we're back again at the same thing. I mean he's already said he didn't know about the article, this portion. I mean, this witness obviously has not seen it, does not know about any of the issues described in this article. It has nothing to do with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He can just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that the witness can answer the question, but that was not the matter raised by Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I may? Just because he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- I ask an opportunity to read the question again. Please tell me what you wanted to tell me, not to already put the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, Your Honour. I apologise. The issue then, of course, he is talking specifically about the article, did he hear about it from anyone else that he may have had contact with. In other words, that was related to this that may have talked about what the Tribunal had decided or not to do -- to do or not do, even if he wasn't aware that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- the original source of that was this article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me take it over at this moment. Mr. Al-Alfi --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of decision-making on the scope of indictments within the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I don't have to ask you what the basis for such knowledge would be, not in any respect, not in relation to this case, not in relation to any other case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm also told at page 52, line 3, I may have misspoken, and it should say that the shelling was occurring at the rate of 10.000 per hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we're talking about 10.000 not about a thousand per hour and I also notice that in --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, just so you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's my --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- that wasn't related to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- my question about -- my question on the transcript, we do not see that I was referring to decision-making on scope of indictments. That is it now then on the record as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will tender the article and then we should MFI because I anticipate we're going to have arguments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A fight over it. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yeah. We're going object, Your Honour, on two separate grounds. First of all is the relevance to this case. It is apparently a report from someone on an internal investigation, internal meeting within the Office of the Prosecutor. And secondly, we have had this issue during Mr. Roberts' testimony about newspaper articles that were not admitted into evidence. And in his objection then, Mr. Misetic said at transcript reference 6843, line 8: "Your Honour, if I may, this now opens the door to everybody going to LexisNexis, finding all the newspaper articles they want and tendering them into evidence as evidence and then telling the other side, Go call the journalists to cross-examine them." I mean, at some point there has to be a line drawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what was the position of the Prosecution at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The position of the Prosecution at that time was that such documents, if they were probative and relevant, could come in. Mr. Waespi made several arguments in that respect, but the Chamber ultimately decided with the Defence, that this article should not be admitted. So we're just seeking some consistency, especially considering that this is -- has no relevance especially not with this witness, who obviously has never seen it and cannot therefore comment on it. At least Mr. Roberts had talk to the journalist, Mr. Fisk, whose article was at issue then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if may I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will go back and find all of the press articles that the OTP since that ruling has tendered into evidence, and on that basis, is -- since the practice has been that they have been tendering newspaper articles, I don't see any reason now for the OTP to take an inconsistent position with what they have been doing since July. And we will go ahead and pull those articles for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The second issue, Mr. President, is the issue is quite relevant in the sense that, as I indicated in our opening arguments and we will repeat them in final arguments but I will give you a relevance. That is this: All of the material -- or I shouldn't say all, most of the material that has now been presented to you regarding the shelling of Knin was in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor by the time the initial indictment review concluded not to include it in an indictment. As I said to you in opening statements, the second -- sorry, the amended indictment against General Gotovina, confirmed in February of 2004, does not contained the words "shelling" or "artillery" anywhere in the entire document. The first time that they came up with a shelling theory was in the joinder indictment in February of 2006. I believe it's entirely proper for the Defence to be able to argue in final argument that the Office of the Prosecutor itself had this information for ten years, in many cases, including the testimonies of General Leslie, General Forand, Mr. Dryer, Mr. Dawes, and the witness who is sitting in the chair, here, at the time they concluded not to include the shelling of Knin in the indictment. Whether ultimately you want to accept that indictment or not, whether the Prosecution agrees with that argument or not, is really irrelevant. It's probative and we're entitled to argue it. And at the end of the day, Your Honour, if the Prosecution -- or if the Chamber concludes that it shouldn't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- come in through this witness, then it is merely a question of whether we're going bar table the exhibit or whether it comes in through this witness. But I also think that these are positions -- this is not simply about the underlying facts and hearsay. These are positions or indications of the positions of a party opponent, much like some of the police reports that have been tendered by the Prosecution, that are hearsay taken in the Croatian police or other hearsay arguments that go towards matters related to the accused in this case. So I think it is admissible, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: May I briefly respond, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You raised the objection. You were able to explain it. Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, it's just about the allegation that all the material the Prosecution presented was available to them ten years ago. That is just not true. We have received information between 1998 and 2006, so I think that's not a relevant portion, and to take one slice of that and then -- and then argue from there that, therefore, there is nothing to support it and they had a solution then, does not make it relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, yes, also half a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Half a minute. Either the Serb civilians left Knin because of shelling or they didn't. To claim now that they discovered ten years later that that was what caused them to leave --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. That is the issue in the case, though. I would also add -- I believe I corrected myself earlier and I said not all but most of the information. And if you look back at the witness transcripts and when they gave statements, I believe I will be found to be correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I haven't heard anything and I do not know to what extent it is relevant, whether there is any Rule 70 issue, here because I see the article is about an internal report which is not under a disclosure obligation. And I do not know how it ended up in the hands of this journalist, whether there's any issue there, if that would be the case, and again I see this article for the first time in my life. I am at page 3 without even having read pages 1 and 2. But it immediately came to my mind and that this is -- and that's not exactly what we saw in earlier press publications that it is dealing with, apparently, an internal work product document within the OTP, which might complicate matters. Mr. Misetic, and I heard you say in a one-liner what the issue was. Sometimes it takes a few more lines to know exactly what the issues are but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if I may again? This is why I suggest we MFI and argue this later because I'm aware that there are some issues. However, I would point out that part of what you will hear in response is that Rule 70 has not been respected with respect to other documents. And I believe I have called that to the attention of the Chamber before when the Prosecution has been tendering documents and they have said, We got this document in the mail anonymously, and therefore we can use it, despite the fact that, say, a document says state secret on it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, I'm talking about 70(A), internal work product.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Whether it is it Rule 54 or whether it's 70(A), the issue is once something in that case gets leaked to the Office of the Prosecutor, or once something gets published in a major media for ten years and there's no objection, there's no action taken by a party to the case to preserve any Rule 70 claim, to now say that the entire world can know it exists and the Trial Chamber can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That also is a complex issue. You know that the best way to draw attention to matters that should not have appeared in publication is to protest against it. That would certainly draw the attention -- well, you're nodding yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you look at the article, Judge, if we scroll down, I can actually show you that the Chief Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we'll first read it. And, Mr. Hedaraly, any further matter on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do believe I need to make this one point if we're talking about Rule 70. The Chief Prosecutor is actually quoted, commenting on the meeting in this article. So to the extent there is protest or to the extent that once leaked the Prosecution acquiesced and participated in the actual commenting on the article, I think is something that the Trial Chamber should consider. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, any need to add anything to what Mr. Misetic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the document to be MFI'd under what number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D1212, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that keeps that status for the time being. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Staying on the topic of shelling, Mr. Al-Alfi, if I could, Mr. Registrar, have Exhibit D29 on the screen. You testified yesterday that you were present and met Mr. Akashi when he came to Knin on the 7th of August. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm going to show you a document. This is Mr. Akashi's memo to Mr. Annan on his trip to Knin on the 7th. And if we go to paragraph 2, he writes to Mr. Annan and says: "My overall impression of the town of Knin is that it suffered considerable damage from artillery fire, which was evident in the streets, where I observed many shops with broken windows, cars damaged and off the road, artillery shell holes in the road, et cetera. However, the damage to the town's structures, while noticeable, was less than I anticipated." And I'll let you read through the rest of the report. But, first of all, do you agree with that assessment by Mr. Akashi as to what you found on your trip to Knin when you actually toured Knin?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a true reflection if you take into consideration that Mr. Akashi toured only a very small part of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not go all over the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, neither did you, then, correct? I mean, you were with Mr. --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on we reported something when we were allowed to go. But at that visit, for your information, even the first time we had the heliport in our headquarters, the first time that we were not allowed even his helicopter to land in our headquarters but it should land somewhere else. So it was only from the heliport, taking him to meeting with officials and those streets what he saw, and then he came to our headquarters to talk and then he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But is it fair to say that on the 7th, you were with Mr. Akashi the entire time?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. So you --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: On the 7th, you didn't see more than Mr. Akashi saw?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that road? Where we parked, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, my question is you were always in the same group?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So it was you, it was Mr. Akashi, do you recall if Mr. Flynn was also present with you?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So it's you, it's Mr. Akashi, it's Mr. Flynn, taking the same tour of Knin together?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true to say the tour of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry. The same trip through Knin together?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same road to meeting the officials in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would put it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, could we seek further clarification about -- especially about the helicopter. You said no permission was given to -- that the helicopter land in the headquarters, I take it then, the compound. Now this Chamber has received some evidence that there was a helicopter -- there was a place for helicopters to land at a sports field not that far away from the headquarters, close to the railway track, and approximately where you take the road to the -- where the road turns to the north, being parallel to the rail track at the railway station. Is that where this helicopter landed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's true, sir. But we used to have helicopter pad inside the headquarters so -- and usually our helicopters land there, but this was the first time that the Croatian authorities insisted that he lands in where you say it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that sports field.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now -- I mean, if we're talking about not a trip through Knin, Mr. Akashi went, accompanied by you, from there to where? Where was the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the headquarters of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shortest route?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, shortest route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is first going west, then turning to the south and then arrive at the compound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now from there, where else did he go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went to meet the officials also in Knin, which is on the main street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the main street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where General Cermak was also stationed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Main street being --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall it. It used to be even used before that for the RSK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the parties could agree on where that is, especially whether that is in the quarters where -- west of the railway station before you have crossed and entered into the remainder part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So could I say the area closest to Knin castle --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- down at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So not entering into the -- not crossing the railway and not going to other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I could follow up on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, do you recall Mr. Akashi and/or Mr. Flynn also going to the hospital on the 7th to assess whether the hospital had been shelled?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it at this moment, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So if it is possible, then Mr. Akashi and/or Mr. Flynn --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I said --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you talk?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, testing 1, 2, 3?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You don't recall whether there was also a trip to the hospital to assess the hospital itself. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it at this moment. Maybe that is it true. But I don't recall it. The exact programme, I don't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you also recall several military attaches from several embassies in Zagreb, coming to Knin on the same day and also touring Knin and including going to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that was an arrangement, it would be have been with the government of Croatia but not through us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you also recall the fact that international media had been allowed into Knin on the 7th of August, while Mr. Akashi was there?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see them, but if they were there, then they were -- this is something between them and the government of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you one of those reports. It's a BBC report from the 7th of August. It is it Exhibit D63.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's coming right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "Reporter: But what is clear is that the Croatians are in control. "Nicolas Witchell: Oh, very much so, yes. Their flags are flying everywhere in this town which only 48 hours ago the Krajina Serbs regarded as their capital now total under the control of the Croatians. The UN say that so far as they can tell, the Croatians have been behaving with discipline and in a correct fashion."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, before I ask you a question let me also read to you what Mr. Flynn said and told this Trial Chamber. This is it at page 1306 at line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, we usually do not refer to testimony of other witnesses until the question has been put to the witness and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think he has addressed in his direct examination but I will -- if you -- he has addressed the issue I want to address in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I do not know what exactly the issue is but if you would follow that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe the procedure is if he has addressed it, just to refer to where in his direct examination then we know and we can compare the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I've actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know yet what the question is, so I have just --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] I'd then prefer to do outside the presence of the witness, but I have a reason for doing my cross-examination this way, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That was the procedure given by the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: -- that if he -- the witness has mentioned it, either in the statement or in direct examination, he should be pointed to where that is and then be impeached and confronted with the new testimony of someone else, just to be fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that's the -- I don't believe that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever it is, Mr. Misetic, you don't have to read it to the witness, but if you give us the reference. I mean, the witness is not able to manipulate the screens whereas we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's page 13809.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me -- first the date, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yesterday. This is just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check it. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, page 13.000 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 809, beginning at line 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And going on to the next page through line 3. And actually you can start earlier, Mr. President, to put it in context, which is starting at line 17, on page 13809.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have found it, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now what Mr. Flynn said with respect to that trip on the 7th was -- the question was: "Mr. Flynn, you were also there on the 7th of August. Do you recall UN personnel saying something to the effect that Croatian forces were behaving professionally and in a correct manner?" His answer was: "I think there was a sense at that time in Knin that they were doing so. I should point out that we got information from some of those 700 displaced persons which filled in the picture, so to speak. But on that first day, the situation seemed relatively stable and under control." Now, do you agree that on that day that Mr. Akashi was in Knin, that the assessment was that the Croatian forces were behaving professionally and in a correct manner?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on how you see professionally. I call General Cermak also a professional. But what he meant by professionally, that's for him to elaborate on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, did you deem the situation on the 7th of August to be stable and under control, in Knin?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under control, in the sense that there is no two parties fighting, yes. But under control, that everything is back to normal, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, the reason I'm asking you these questions, Mr. Al-Alfi, is that yesterday you testified at page 13.809, beginning at line 23, that: "On that day, we observed at least ten or 11 houses on fire in town."

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can you explain why that fact wasn't in Mr. Akashi's report, wouldn't have been noted in a BBC report, wasn't mentioned by Mr. Flynn? Do you have any explanation why they might have not seen what you saw on that day?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They saw what I saw, and Mr. Akashi himself, as I reported, took it with the officials immediately. And if you notice from the earlier questioning that even when we talk after the 20th, there were some houses still being burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm talking about 7th August.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm just telling you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could have 1D00-0745, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, this is a report by Mr. Akashi from the 10th of August to Mr. Annan, and it reports on his meeting with the ICFY co-chairman, which, as you know, were Mr. Stoltenberg and Mr. Bildt, and had this meeting in Zagreb on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if I could have page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The paragraph that begins: "The co-chairmen were keen for detailed information on the humanitarian situation in the sectors ..." And then if we scroll -- go down a little bit to the middle to the sentence that begins: "They wished to know -- to also know." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "They wished to also know what we would do with the information we were currently receiving on human rights abuses and asked whether such information would be conveyed to The Hague." Now, as someone who worked in civil affairs, do you know or have any information or -- I should say, can you recollect, when was the first time that you recall hearing that this institution, the ICTY, may be interested in investigating Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not for me to decide, because that was the SRSG. That was his opinion and what he wants to follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Actually, this --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, in his later --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's actually one of the co-chairmen or both co-chairmen --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in Akashi's report. That's what I'm saying. In Akashi's message. I did not say this is the first time I see it, but that's for Akashi to answer, not for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about you personally. Did you ever, while you were in Sector South, after Operation Storm, hear that the ICTY may be investigating this case?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that was -- at that time it was too early even to talk about it. Because we were only observing and reporting at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if we go to the next paragraph, please. On more generals topics, the second sentence says: "Granic," and that refers to the Croatian Foreign Minister. "Granic had also indicated ..." It's the third line in the paragraph that begins: "On more general topics."

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says: "Granic had also indicated that the Croatian military plan had been designed to facilitate their departure, a form of ethnic cleansing by other means, in Mr. Bildt 's opinion. With regard to the swift routing of the ARSK, it was felt that this had been a result of the Croatians taking the ARSK by surprise with new military tactics. The HV targeting of command and control elements, the taking of high ground and the intensive use of heavy artillery on towns had been unanticipated. In effect, the Croatians had used the past few years to prepare for a professional military assault, while the ARSK had continued to focus on past tactics. However, despite reports to the contrary, it was the ICFY's understanding that the ARSK had mounted a fierce defence of Knin and had had no intention of abandoning the town ..." Now, I'm going to refer to this document again after I show you the next document. But before I do that, was it also your understanding that the intention of the ARSK was to mount a fierce defence of Knin? Did you know?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Talking? Yes. Even they reaffirmed it the night [Realtime transcript read in error "9th"] -- if you see from my previous statement, when we met them the night they asked the demands. They were saying, Yes, we want the families, but we will be here, we will be resisting, yes, talking, but what abilities they have, I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm interested in this because this is a meeting on the 9th of August and it talks about the targeting -- that the HV targeted command and control elements, took high ground and intensively used heavy artillery on towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And first, Mr. President, I tender this exhibit before I move on to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1213, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1213 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have Exhibit D1210, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, this is tab 5 in your binder. Just for the sake of the transcript -- Mr. Al-Alfi, you don't have to worry about this. For the sake of the transcript at page 69, line 10, if the Chamber doesn't mind, I don't think he said even they reaffirmed it on the 9th. I believe he said on the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I understood as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, I'm interested in the second paragraph on this page. And there the third sentence says and I quote -- let's start with the second sentence. This is your report and it says the: "Croatian offensive mainly centred on Knin with several thousand" --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Second paragraph, second sentence.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "The Croatian offensive mainly centred on Knin with several thousands of impacts, although now it appears that certain targets were subject to greater shelling, such as the fuel supply depot and Knin radio station. Some of the shelling could be described as indiscriminate and resulted in casualties and damage amongst civilians and their property." I'm interested in the way you phrased that sentence because it's -- you wrote "although it now appears," and this is a report of the 11th of August, which suggests to me that after the 4th, the appearance somehow -- you obtained more information than when you were there on the 4th. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, yes. Every day we get more information and we were out and we started seeing also things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. What -- do you recall, can you tell us exactly what additional information you obtained that then allowed you to say that it now appears that certain targets were subject to greater shelling?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because by seeing some of the damage, that why I mentioned some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So you're just referring to your own personal --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not personal. Not personal. I have my own civil affairs officers who are touring the area. We started being allowed to move in the city, so they come and report to me what they saw, and the military also were moving. So they could -- I mean, not as freedom completely, but they could observe it and report it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, some of your civil affairs officers, do you recall the names of the people -- of these civil affairs officers who reported this information back to you?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them report to me. All -- all the civil affairs -- because I was the -- literally the head civil affairs coordinator, that means heading all this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I mean which of them gave you the information --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall specific, but all of them they come and report to me, and it is not a secret. The UN knows who were the people working for me at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. This statement that the shelling resulted in casualties and damage amongst civilians and their property. Civilian bodies, including children and women were seen in the streets of Knin. You didn't observe children, the bodies of children in the streets of Knin, did you?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But as I said in my statement also, the day, the day we were called to the RSK it was the first day. When we stepped out of the APC, I saw with my own eyes some civilians, dead bodies on the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what were they dressed in?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Like -- can you describe the clothes?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shirt and normal shirts and -- but not the military -- I would consider that a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not count them because we had to jump out of the APC to go to the meeting. It was -- they -- the whole area was still under shelling, but if I recollect correctly, just next to us where we stop the APC there were around 10, 11 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Where did you stop the APC?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the main street, where it used to be the RSK headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So these were bodies of people located next to the RSK headquarters?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, in the street, just before. Not at the headquarters itself. The headquarters had no compound. It was on the main street. You jump from the car to the door and you go in. So it was the main street used, and we stopped our APC -- you know, inside the APC we don't see. We have only small things, small windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And how many -- how many metres was it from the ARSK headquarters?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say around 40, 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And is there a reason that this observation doesn't appear in any of your reporting or General Forand's reporting?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I mean on the 4th, or the 5th, or the 6th.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not meant to say -- I mean, we were not talking -- at that time we were talking how to meet the overall situation, not counting bodies at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you had seen these bodies and you were travelling with General Forand, would General Forand have also seen these bodies?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I expect, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss it with General Forand?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He already saw them. To discuss what? How they were killed? We knew that the area was under shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you raise the issue with the ARSK authorities as to why they were leaving bodies in the street?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, the area -- still the area was under shelling. We were called only for a certain purpose, with their demand that they want fuel and all that. It was no time to discuss anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did anybody say, We should call an ambulance or transport these people to a hospital?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: An ambulance? Nobody was moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That doesn't mean they're dead, does it?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dead bodies, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not moving. They were lying down in the street. They were dead bodies. I could see some of them in bad shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now let me ask you -- let me draw your attention to page 42 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we start at page 24 [sic] and this is where you talk about these bodies. And you say: "You saw them on the main street, they were -- at least if I'm not mistaken, they open the door and we were about to go to the meeting. I was looking and there were quite a number of dead bodies in the main street. I mean, if I'm not mistaken at least between 10 and 15. And then you were asked: "Did you take a close look at those bodies? "Answer: No. "Could you say how those people were killed? "Answer: Because as I told you, we just left the APC, and for security purposes, we have to rush into the building because we cannot -- it was not fun at this time." If you go to the next page: "What else did you see between moving from the APC and the military area? "Answer: As I told you, the APC was immediately in front of the -- I saw a number of houses on the main street burned by shelling," and then it goes on. So what you said here was, first, you agree that you didn't take a close look at the bodies. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Second, you don't know how those people were killed?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But I took it that because of the shelling. But I did not know, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Third, when you saw what you believed to be bodies, it was as you were exiting the APC and entering the ARSK headquarters building?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And whatever you saw would have been at least at a distance of 50 metres because, as you told me, these bodies -- alleged bodies were 50 metres from the ARSK headquarters?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I correct you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we saw, as you might say, 40 or 50 metres. Besides I told you the APCs have small windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's not what you said here.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just telling you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: While passing we saw also through that small window, but when they opened the door, we saw the dead bodies exactly from a distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You agree with me that's not what you said in 1998?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said what I said in 1998, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: All right. If I could take you to -- just a few more questions. Yesterday at page 13.822, lines 16 to 18, Mr. Russo was asking you some questions about a report concerning someone from the Croatian Red Cross, and you said -- and it concerned the issue of prisoners of war, and I believe you say that they believe that this man from the Croatian Red Cross in Zadar confirmed to -- that to them they are prisoner of war especially those who were in military uniform of the RSK. Were there persons inside the UN camp in military uniform? I mean, outside the UN personnel. Were there Serbs in the UN camp, beginning on the evening of the 4th of August, that were in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When people came to the camp --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- they were mostly civilians. Yes, there were some with military uniform. But the condition of the UN to allow them in was two conditions. One, all weapons, if they have any, and they should be searched and the weapon should be handed to the UN. This was the first condition. Second condition, that they would be provided with civilian clothes and they should not stay inside the camp with their military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How many of those types of individuals were there?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly, but they were a very small number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If I could take you to tab 11 in your folder or binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which is 65 ter 4179, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a report from the 1st of September that you wrote.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we go to the last page, which is page 6 in the English. You write: "Furthermore, our office in Zadar reported that Croatians are being moved quickly to resettle in the villages and towns. The building of destroyed houses and properties and the clearing of mines have started. Croatian officials hope that most of the displaced persons will be resettled back in their communities within the next two months. Hotels and resort areas are also rehabilitating and refurbishing their properties that had become refugee centres. All this is in preparation for the next tourist season. Obviously, the hopes and expectations for renewed economic activities in this area are quite high." Can you -- do you have any knowledge or information that you can share with us about why the Croatians wanted to move these people out of the hotels and tourist resorts and move them into the newly liberated areas?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all let me tell you -- I mean, when we talk here, we're not talking about Knin itself only. We're talking about the whole sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay? Because the hotels and resorts were not in Knin itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I just want you to be aware of it. So some of those areas were hosting refugees, all right, and they want them, as I said, because they started, even on the media, talking about refurbishing the tourism in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But were you aware that the Croatian government had a desire to move people and house them in the liberated areas and get them out of refugee centres?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we saw some already in action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Al-Alfi, I'm just going to show you one video which is a follow-up on some answers that you gave to Mr. Kay this morning, and it relates to the issue of translators or interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could I have 1D00-0749. It is a video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is not in e-court yet because it just came up as result of your testimony this morning, Mr. Al-Alfi.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I just don't know about the 4179. It's on the Prosecution's list, but I don't know if Mr. Misetic wants to move it in as a Defence exhibit or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you strike it from your list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. We tender it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 4179 becomes Exhibit D1214.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1214 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we've disclosed the audio and the video to the Prosecution, but we have no need for the audio. So we won't be playing the audio or tendering it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you do not play the audio, there's no need to have it translated. We just look at the pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, this is a visit to Knin by Mr. Akashi on the 5th of June, 1995, and he is holding talks with Mr. Martic, and I believe you were in the delegation --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, when did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 5th of June?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. This is it wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It could be later in June --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be later because I arrived in Knin on the 9th or 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay, well, then I will check the date, but it's definitely 1995.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be June, yes. I think the date definitely has to be after the 9th because I arrived 9th or 10th June in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honour, it's because the issue only came up this morning, so we've tried to put this together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, looking at the first picture it says the 5th of June. So unless --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If it's wrong, we'll change it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who put it there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We put it that on the top --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You put it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have to apologise. I was reminded before by the registrar that, Mr. Misetic, that we are making the same mistakes, as many others do, that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. JUDGE ORIE -- you immediately make the mistake again, that is to speak at the same time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for lumping yourself in with me, Mr. President. If we could go head and play this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If the date is wrong we will of course make the change, but I believe you are present for this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is that you behind Mr. Akashi?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the one on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. So we will check the date. But I just want to show you the pictures and ask you to identify certain individuals, if you can. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the person sitting at the far end of the table? Do you recall him at all?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of Sabo Strbac?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only one I recall, but not by name, the one with the suit. He used to call himself the president of -- yeah, that one I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Al-Alfi. The gentleman sitting at the far end of this table, and I could be wrong, but it looks like directly across from you. Is that you at the end of the table?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I could be wrong. But you recall --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I cannot sit on this side. I'm on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I meant, you see the person looking towards the camera at the end of this table?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And then there's someone sitting across from him?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the picture clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know that individual?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We can skip to the one-minute mark. Right there. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The person behind Mr. Martic on the left-hand side, do you remember him?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alun Roberts?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. But I don't recall his face. It has been 13 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This individual on the right, in the delegation where you are, is named Predrag Sare. Do you recall that name?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We'll skip forward then. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is that you in the back corner, back right --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- it's not clear. To me, it's here not clear. But it can be, but I cannot say definitely yes, me. But I was with the delegation on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Were you ever told that there was an issue in the UN Sector South about an interpreter being employed in the sector despite the fact that it was known that he had, at least in the past, worked for Serbian intelligence?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not told.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you know if this interpreter in fact, even after Operation Storm, was present in the compound and continued to provide interpretation for persons in the -- officials in the UN compound?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- he did not work for me, at least definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we will tender the video into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Frankly, Your Honour, I fail to see what the relevance of it is. I mean, we'll review the audio --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least we know who Mr. Al-Alfi does not know --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm not sure that assists the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- while I don't know how -- well, I think, as such it has been shown to Mr. Al-Alfi and he has given some answers, and I think it would be appropriate to have it in evidence, if only for later comparison if any other witness comes and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may just say -- obviously, as I said, we hadn't prepared this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- for today, but it came up, and in case it is an issue later, it should be in evidence in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Not because it gives us a lot of information, but you would say it could be MFI'd for that purpose as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, exactly. Especially because the witness's testimony is that there were interpreters before but not after. And this is a June video, it doesn't really do anything with the witness, but, I mean, we can MFI it. It's not a major --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is, I think, undisputed amongst the parties that Mr. Sare continued to be an interpreter after Operation Storm, so I'm not sure what the basis is for that objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not spend too much time on it. Mr. Registrar, the number of this exhibit would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is becomes Exhibit D1215.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have one additional question, Mr. Al-Alfi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But after I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- given the decision of the Chamber that Exhibit D1215 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi you never sought a meeting with General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he has to press the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, we have to ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, you never sought a meeting with General Gotovina after Operation Storm. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is a military. As I told you, we have to understand the structure. If anyone to seek a meeting with, it was General Forand, but I saw him once, or twice, by coincidence. I was with General Cermak and he was there, but for a few minutes. I had nothing to discuss with him. I am discussing with the man in front of me who I'm told that he is charge of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, are you ready to cross-examine Mr. Al-Alfi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I am. I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll first have a break, and could you give us your final estimate on time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I would say 45 minutes, Your Honour, at the most. I have three -- I have basically three to four themes to cover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Five minutes. We will then have break and resume at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Kuzmanovic is counsel for Mr. Markac. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Al-Alfi.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to take you back to what you talked about in your cross-examination with Mr. Misetic. On page 75, lines 10 to 21, you were asked some questions about what you saw while you were in the APC going toward the ARSK headquarters building. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, you'll not find it because Mr. Kuzmanovic is referring.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the transcript of today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If I'm referring to your transcript, Mr. Al-Alfi, I will let you know.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You were asked a question about what you saw, and you said you could see out of a window in the APC bodies out in the street. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now you can refer to your statement, Mr. Al-Alfi. I'll take to you page 30 of your statement, your written statement, which is, I believe, P1160. And the investigator was asking you some questions related to that same issue in your statement back in March of 1995. On line 7, you were asked: "When you were being transported in the APC, could you see anything outside." And your answer was: "No, because the APC did not," and then it says, "/unclear/ windows." And this statement, this is what you gave in 1998. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the statement I gave in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Al-Alfi, I'd like to ask you some questions related to your role --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, I'm wondering whether there is confusion here. I'm just looking at the context, because it is my recollection that -- no, let me not -- Mr. Hedaraly, you were on your feet. I will refrain from any comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I just think that the unclear reference in the interview, I think, that is the tape did not properly capture what the witness said. So I think just for the sake of clarity he should be asked if he remembers what he said then because he said did not something the windows. We don't know what it is, and since Mr. Kuzmanovic wants to refer to it, I think perhaps we can ask the witness if he remembers what he meant in that sentence.
