utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, it's -- you can correct me if I'm wrong, but at least of 1998, your answer on line 9 to the question of whether you could see anything outside the APC was no, because the APC did not, and I am assuming the word there is "have windows." Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, APCs have windows, so I would not assume that they don't have windows. They have very small windows you can see through. But if you ask about seeing -- that an open area seeing, the APC was moving. That's what I meant. It was moving. But I saw quickly that through that window until it stopped, I saw some dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What other word could you fit in there other than "did not" -- other than the word "have" for sentence to make any sense? If you can tell me?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, if you look the overall statement, okay, although I studied in London university, there are some -- because when you talk to somebody it's different, that it can be disconnected --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But -- but.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Al-Alfi. I'm not being critical of you at all, in any way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, we can ask the witness what he said at the time, whether if he remembers, what to fit in logically is not something a witness -- if he doesn't remember what he said, I could give you five answers to that question, all very logical. I don't think you want to hear --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honour, I'll challenge you -- I'll challenge you to give me five answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. At a later stage, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, I'll move on, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, I'd like to ask you some questions generally related to your job in Sector South -- or in Knin, I should say. Can you describe for me what you did before Operation Storm in your role. Who did you meet with, what kind of reporting did you undertake, generally, before Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was reassigned to Sector South, as we used to call it, not only Knin. Knin was our headquarters to be in charge. And as civil affairs coordinator, which I told you later on the name of the post was changed to be political and humanitarian affairs coordinator. If I'm not mistaken, I arrived in there on 9th or 10th June. It was only one day later after an incident happened to one of our UN military at that time, a Kenyan. He was killed. And my job to be -- was to be, according to our structure, we had the military side and the civilian side. The military side is led by the Sector Commander, as we call it. Usually he is a General. And equal to him was the civil affairs coordinator to deal with the civilian matters. It was mostly civil affairs, and the word "civil affairs" is, I can understand it, it is mostly used in the American system and that's why it appeared first in the Vance Plan. In other words, humanitarian, providing assistance to civilians, caring about civilians, and reporting also these cases to our headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the same methodology, Mr. Al-Alfi, in terms of daily reporting that you had after Operation Storm, meaning that would you have a daily report that you'd send to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the situation. Sometimes, yes. It used to be daily reporting. Sometimes -- but a must was weekly reporting. A must. That's -- even if you report daily, you have at the end of the week to summarize what you were the developments during the week and your assessment, because it is daily, like, meetings which happen or incidents what happened throughout that week. But at the end of the week, we had to submit what we used to call weekly report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in the course of a week, would you have regular meetings with the ARSK milicija or civilian police?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Police will be met by UNCIVPOL, not by me. But with the authorities at that time, in there, don't forget, yes, I used to have but not necessarily weekly, whenever we had problems to discuss, and they had their own problems. Everybody is aware of them. There was also a breakdown of the system itself between Sector East and Sector South, the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when you -- you mentioned an UNCIVPOL would be in charge of dealing with the local police. Were you someone who would oversee UNCIVPOL or would UNCIVPOL report to you things and then you would report them to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. They would copy to me. Not report to me, and if there are cases of civilians I would also ask them to go and do that job or check that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So if someone came to you before Operation Storm occurred and said, There are civilians in a certain village or a certain hamlet that need assistance, either humanitarian or otherwise, you would then direct that request to UNCIVPOL or a humanitarian organisation to fulfil that request.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I would ask my civil affairs officer who is -- you know, we had a division, we had civil affairs officers who are in charge of certain areas, a division of labour. I would ask him to go, if necessary, to go with the UNCIVPOL, and if it is the information I feel that it is serious, I may ask even the military to accompany them, just to make sure that they are safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look for an example. If there was a crime that had occurred before Operation Storm to, let's say, at that point someone who was in the Croatian minority in June of 1995, would that crime be reported to the local police?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And would that be the similar methodology you would have taken after Operation Storm, that if you saw that a crime or crimes had occurred or potential crimes that those things should be reported to the civil police?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes, and not necessarily a crime. To give you a good example, at one point our headquarters received a request from the Croatian government that there were two old ladies, I mentioned it in my statement, two old ladies over 80, and they needed treatment in Croatia proper, and I had to go and talk to authorities there and arrange until they accepted even that a UN helicopter will come to the pad to carry them all the way to Zagreb. I just want you to know. Civilian matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to state that if there was a crime that you became aware of or that someone made you aware of, that it would not be the regular course or procedure for that issue not to be reported to the police but to be reported to someone else?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a confusing question. I will rephrase it. It's fair to state, is it not, that the regular procedure that should have been followed by anyone in UN civilian affairs that you had any control over or any UNCIVPOL matter -- person, for that matter, that if there was a crime that occurred that you were made aware of, that it must be reported to whatever local police are there at the particular time. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. If we received such information we will inform them, and we will report it to our headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware -- you may have been asked and if you were, I'm sorry. Were you aware of the specific structure of how the local police was organised after Operation Storm in Sector South?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe our UNCIVPOL knew about it but not me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So if a report came to you about a crime that might have occurred who would you then report that to? If you --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean after or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: After Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a report came to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- at that time we only had one power. Okay? If we observed something or something reported to us, to convey it to the headquarters and to take it with the new authorities in Knin, which is General Cermak and -- or UNCIVPOL will take with the civil police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So there would be instances, then, in which potentially crimes that occurred were not reported to the police. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself, Mr. Al-Alfi, take any -- strike that. You yourself, Mr. Al-Alfi, did not take any measures to confirm the accuracy of the reports you submitted other than perhaps in meetings that yourself had attended. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you take any measures to confirm the accuracy of the reporting that was brought to you for you to submit to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which other measures you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go try to confirm some of the reports that were given to you or were you simply someone who got a report, put it in your report, and passed it up to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the incident, but we had no means of confirming or not confirming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you were basically a pass-through person who would be getting information and passing that information on to Zagreb for the most part?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- correct because I depend, as I said, on my civil affairs officers who go, sometimes they see and sometimes reported to them. And then come to me, I sit with them, I check it, and if I find that it is worth being forwarded I do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So in other words, the reports that you wrote -- the accuracy of the reports you wrote depended upon the accuracy of the information that you received. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I trust my civil affairs officers. And I trust the UNCIVPOL.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If you could go to page 105 of your transcript -- of your statement, I should say, P1160. Before I talk to you about this passage, and let me know when you found it, Mr. Al-Alfi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, page 105.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In this particular passage, starting at line 12, the question before your answer was that: "Did you personally observe any person being intimidated?" And part of your answer was: "As a civil affairs coordinator, I rarely observed anything. You can even say zero. As the civil affairs coordinator, I'm in the headquarters. I am the -- the centre where all this information comes to me and then I reflect what is important, what is not important." It's fair to state, is it not, Mr. Al-Alfi, that the information that you got was not based on personal observation. It was based on information you received?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are talking about the overall situation, yes. But there were some instances, the ones I mentioned earlier, when I was on the APC, yes, I observed it myself. But if you talk about this, yes, the civil affairs coordinator is to deal with the civilian or whatever authorities, political, let's call it, authorities. But it's my civil affairs officers who would report to me, and this confirms what I said earlier to you, that I would sit with the civil affairs officer and check. That's why if I see it not important, hearsay or something like that, I would not forward it because I see that the information is not complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Al-Alfi, you were in Knin until when?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until it closed, the whole mission closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So that was when, in 1996?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall correctly, but, yes, 1996. And I still remember even I am the one who handed over our headquarters to the Croatian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you would agree with me, Mr. Al-Alfi, that while you were in Knin and in the surrounding areas of Sector South, you never personally observed arson. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arson?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, arson.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I observed it. I saw the houses on fire, yes, but I did not see people doing it. Who were doing it, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go to your -- page 105 of your interview, Mr. Al-Alfi, line 31.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Line?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the question is: "Whilst you were in Knin and the surrounding areas of Sector South, did you personally observe arson, somebody lighting a fire to a home?" And you had answered no.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said now. I confirmed it. I said seeing somebody burning a house, I did not see it, but I saw the house on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that you did not personally observe people looting but you observed goods in vehicles. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. There were some military and some civilian vehicles. I said it yesterday, and today I repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please call up 65 ter 4179.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe that's D1214.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think it is in tab 11 of the binder for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, in the first paragraph of this document, under the section that's called "Message," the date of it is September 1st of 1995. The last sentence of that first paragraph, when you're talking about burning of houses and looting, you say: "In some cases, Croatian army personnel and special police forces were seen very close to the sites of such incidents but taking no action to stop such activities." I wanted to ask you specifically about special police forces that are mentioned in this report. Have you ever spoken with anyone in the special police forces?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me personally. This is -- as I told you, the system, my officers report and maybe they did speak to them or not, I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You yourself have never spoken to anybody?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen, yourself, the special police forces?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, while they are -- but I did not talk to them. They have a special dress. It's a special uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What did they look like?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot describe it correctly, but it was different from what used to be the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What colour?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It can be blue, it can be dark grey, something like that. But I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know where -- where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, in the streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In Knin?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give me any dates or places or times that you refer to special police forces being close to sites of such incidents?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have specific dates, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Or specific --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall at this time specific dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And there are no specific dates, places or times in any of these reports, that you're aware of, correct, with regard to the special police?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There might be in the reports of my colleagues who reported to me, but, now, we are talking only about my own reports which are the culmination of all those reports, but there might be specific details there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In any event, in this report there are no details?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in this report there are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: How often did you get outside of Knin while you were in Sector South?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean outside of Knin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Outside of the Knin municipality. Did you travel to places like Obrovac, Gracac or Donji Lapac, during your time?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, almost -- every week I have to make a tour. If I am in charge of a sector, I have to know what is at least the situation inside the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have a chance to go to Gracac?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you meet with in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not meet anyone but I mean going to the areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Croatian government had named as a special commissioner for Gracac a man by the name of Ivan Prpic?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You had said that you met with Mr. Pasic, who was the Croatian government special representative of the commissioner for Knin; correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Knin. That's why I met him in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. But you had no such meeting with any other specific government commissioner in any other area --

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe my civil affairs officers did, but personally I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to your reporting, Mr. Al-Alfi, at least from the reports that you have -- that had been compiled for you. There are no reports relating to, for example, Gracac or Donji Lapac? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the focus was on the Knin area in particular and what was going on. There might -- and don't forget, our movement was not as easy, although under the title freedom of movement -- I mentioned it in a number of reports that freedom of movement does not mean as it is literally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. I guess I'm not talking specifically just about the first few weeks of August of 1995. I am talking about your entire time-frame that you were in Sector South.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean before or after?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: After Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, after that period my -- personally my main focus was how to deal. That's why you will see even so much of the reporting that immediately followed was how to deal with those who were -- who took refuge in our headquarters and how to sort out this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, I'd like to you go to -- --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, please call up 65 ter 4126. You know what? I'll skip that document. Let's go to 65 ter 4163, please. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which number is it in my folder?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it's in your folder, Mr. Al-Alfi. This was a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not see it on the exhibit list presented by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It should show up on your screen, Mr. Al-Alfi.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On the right is the B/C/S version, and I'll just represent to you that the cover page notes that this document came from you, in terms of being forwarded. The second page of this document, which is dated August 28th of 1995, deals with a Human Rights Action Team report which described the surrender of 10 of 14 RSK soldiers still hiding in the area 12 kilometres from Knin. You were familiar with this incident. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you see this report, and I said throughout in my testimony, the Human Rights Action Teams had their direct responsibility -- as you will even notice in my testimony, I said the Human Rights Action Team had direct responsibility to what was established at the headquarters in Zagreb. There they established something called Human Rights Action Cell, if I'm not mistaken, and I still remember even the name of the person who was in charge of that cell. Her name is Peggy Hicks, in Zagreb. So their reporting was direct, that's why you will notice in such a report I cannot change except forward because when they report -- because I'm in the sector also they report -- they copy me. They have to copy me. So if you notice, without talking about the contents, they are the ones to be asked about the contents, not me. I had to forward it because I forward it to our part of the headquarters which is the civil affairs or the political and humanitarian affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Just so I'm clear, Mr. Al-Alfi, you forwarded this report but the substance of the report itself, you had nothing to do with, and you were simply relying on the report of a Human Rights Action Team to give you the information to forward?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Irrespective of that, if you could take a look at paragraph 2 of the document. Irrespective of that forwarding that you did, were you aware that, on the 28th of August, the RSK soldiers surrendered to a platoon of Croatian special police soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about it exactly as I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So other than reading it and hearing about it in the report, you had no other independent knowledge regarding this?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of similar surrenders and RSK soldiers, pockets of them in various places throughout Sector South shortly after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall correctly. I mean, exactly, but if it -- anything it will be reported either by the Human Rights Action Teams and I would forward it, if it ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you have no independent knowledge?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D1216.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1216 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Al-Alfi, we had some discussion earlier on in your cross-examination about daily reporting, and I'd like to know from you -- we've had a chance, obviously, to look through most, if not all, of your reports and those that you forwarded and those that you had put together from reports that were given to you. On August 25th, 26th, 27th, and 28th, those are four days for which there are no daily reports, and I was just wondering if you could explain to us what the reason might be that there weren't daily reports for those four consecutive days.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall every single report I sent. There might be. Because even I heard here that not all the reports -- some of the other reports were quoted and they said, It is not in your folder. So, I don't know. I cannot recall exactly whether I reported or not, on those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it your practice and procedure and habit to report each day following Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not a practice, I mean, but because of the situation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And as far as you know, and just so I'm perfectly clear, for those four days there may be reports, there may not be reports. You simply don't know?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Al-Alfi, ever have any personal contact with any member of the Croatian special police from the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not get your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I certainly can. Mr. Al-Alfi, did you yourself, personally, ever have any contact with any member of the Croatian special police of the Ministry of Interior of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Knin or outside of Knin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Anywhere.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's fair to say that you've never met or spoke with General Markac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: My statement is correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. That's what I meant by yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you to refer to your transcript again -- or your statement again, I'm sorry, P1160. I'll get you a page reference in just a second. Page 108, and we're looking at line 20.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Page 108.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Line 20.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the interviewer is thanking you for your time and asks you a question about your voluntary participation, and I just have a question about your part of your answer. You say: "Oh, yes, and as I told you, my understanding of it is how to contribute to your success because it is also a part of my responsibility. And after you have clarified exactly what was the purpose." Could you explain to me what you meant by being part -- having responsibility to be part of "your success"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, to me, this phrase what I meant is by helping to you do your job.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN AL-ALFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it's part of my responsibility because my responsibility, when I was in -- as in my capacity as coordinator of the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 92.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You gave a fairly long answer, Mr. Al-Alfi, and I won't get into most of the answer, but for some context, I'll just generally summarize what the discussion was. The discussion was dealing with civilian and political authorities in Croatia and in Zagreb, and you were speaking about Mr. Cermak here. And on line 25, you state: "So he knew that the situation turned to be not military. It's more of a civilian and it causes them embarrassment internationally, so maybe with me he had been very careful and tried to show that he is forthcoming." And that next line, the question is: "What do you mean that it's more embarrassing civilian-wise? Could you explain this for me, the purpose, the significance?" And you answer: "Because the whole international focus and international attention was more on the civilian now. Part of what happened with," and it's unclear, "with burning, with looting, rather than -- they're not military operations at all. They are not talking about cease-fire. So it's no more a military operation." And I'd just want you, if you could, to clarify your answer to that, and you can tell me if I'm wrong or not. Was it your position in answering this question that the issue with burning and looting was primarily a civilian issue and not a military issue?

As far as I understand it, and I stand to be corrected, I meant here the military operations are no more going on. Now, we see burning of houses. We see -- we -- we see our reports some people found killed and we talk about looting. So these are civilian matters. I mean, to me, the situation is no more the military operation. That means the shelling all these things or fighting, has stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And so as far as you're concerned, the issue with burning and looting is something that's a civilian issue, at this point in time?
Civilian in the sense that it is targeting civilians. That's what I meant by civilian issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that the people who are conducting this, whether they're military or civilian, it's a civilian issue to deal with?
Well, that's my basic understanding. But it's not for me to judge. It's for legal matters to be -- to decide whether they are civilian or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Al-Alfi. Thank you very much. I don't have any further.
Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If you can go back to tab 11 in your binder, that is at D1214, and you were asked some questions this morning, just now by Mr. Kuzmanovic and earlier by Mr. Misetic, and I just want to make sure that I understood your answers correctly. If you can go to the last page of that document, the last paragraph to which Mr. Mr. Misetic had referred to.
Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: About the refugees being resettled. Let me just find the exact question you were asked. It's at page 78 of the draft transcript: "But you were aware that the Croatian government had a desire to move people and house them in the liberated areas and get them out of refugee centres?" You answered: "Well, we saw some already in action." And if we look at the report, the first sentence: "Furthermore, our office in Zadar reported that Croatians are being moved quickly to resettle in their village and towns." Can you tell the Chamber who was being resettled in terms of refugees, were they Croat refugees or Serb refugees?
What I meant here?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

In 1990/1991 when the war started, there were some Croats in these areas. They were -- they left the area. They turned to be refugees in what used to be called Croatia proper, not in the United Nations protected areas. These refugees who lived all those years outside the sector were brought back. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Al-Alfi. If I can have P363 on the screen. You don't have that in your package. It's going to come on the screen. And I want to ask you -- while the document is being loaded I can ask you. Can you tell the Court who Mr. Pitkanen was?
According to our chain of command, he was like -- you can say my direct boss in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go to page 5 of that document, please. This a letter --
Which one -- which one are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Of course. The one on the screen.
On the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The one on the screen, the letter in front of you now on the screen --
Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: -- by General Forand. The first sentence -- it's dated 11 August 1995, as you can see. The first sentence: "During our meeting yesterday, both Mr. Paavo Pitkanen and I brought to your attention," that is to Mr. Cermak," information gathered by UN sources concerning the widespread and systematic looting and destruction of property, crops and live stock." Let me just pause a second for the translation. And my question for you is: Were you present at that meeting with General Forand and Mr. Pitkanen, on the 10th of August, the day before this letter was sent?

I don't recall correctly but most probably, yes. Because he's -- according to the chain of command, he is my boss, Pitkanen. So unless I had something else, I would have been there, with them, and you notice one thing which is very important from this letter. Most of the letters we are dealing military to military, so most of the letters, if any, would go from our headquarters, would go from General Forand to General Cermak not from me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So this would be an instance, on the 10th of August, when you met General Cermak and notified him about the looting and burning but that was not reflected in one of your reports that was shown to you earlier today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The witness said probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: With that proviso, that would be accurate?
That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have no more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly. Mr. Al-Alfi, you remember the questions about the 10.000 shots fired in an hour. Could you -- do you remember and could you give us an indication about the frequency of hearing impacts? Let me try to give you guidance. Was it more like boing boing boing boing boing, or was it more like boing, boing. Could you give us an impression of what you heard rather than asking you to judge upon the competence of other persons. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It's more of the first expression you gave, and even the boing boing boing -- from different directions. It's not only one boing. It is all over the place, to the extent that even our headquarters, which used to be just in the corner, was shaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you say it is was even more. Would that be baba baba baba, like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just -- for the parties I'm just trying to understand, knowing, reducing what 10.000 an hour means in a second. I try to -- rather than to seek a judgement, to seek your memory on this matter. Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think for the purpose of the record, I don't know if this is some evidence that Your Honours wanted to preserve but as to the frequency --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As far as the -- first of all, if you would listen to the audio, you will know what it is. That's one. I think I started with a frequency of two in a second, at least every bang less than -- far less than a second; whereas my second example was approximately one bang in every, I would say, three to four seconds, but if anyone disagrees, then listen to the audio. The reason why I did it because the average on 10.000 an hour would be two to three in a second. Thank you for your answer. Have the questions in re-direct or the questions from the Bench triggered any need to put further questions to Mr. Al-Alfi? That not being the case, Mr. Al-Alfi, I'm glad that we were able to conclude your testimony today. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe trip home again. Yes, Mr. Al-Alfi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, may I have a personal request? It is up to the Court to grant me or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether I'm even in a position or whether the Court is in a position to grant it, but tell us what your request would be, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because General Cermak is a man I dealt with, can I shake hands with him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that is not usually not done, Mr. Al-Alfi, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is -- no, but the mere fact that you asked for it certainly is understood by Mr. Cermak. So to that extent, it's -- whether you would call that a virtual handshake or something like that, I do not know. But it's on the record. He has heard what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Al-Alfi out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as tomorrow and the day after tomorrow is concerned, the Chamber knows that the courtroom will be available tomorrow in the afternoon and the Chamber would like to receive, as quickly as possible, any further objections against the course which would take us to tomorrow morning, tomorrow in the afternoon and Friday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have been able to read the third statement now and assess notes made by my team on the matter. Ms. Higgins will actually deal with the cross-examination, but we do not anticipate it will be a long time. It would be under 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The other parties, could they give an estimate? Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Roughly the same, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would say two, two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then one hour for you, two and a half hours -- that would mean that we'd need --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Hour and a half, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Hour and a half, yes. That would mean that we would need two sessions. Experience tells us that it is, although not today, that it's usually getting worse than better. Of course the Chamber will have to decide whether or not to cancel the extra session Thursday afternoon. Of course, another way of proceeding would be to see whether we can finish in that extra session and then not to sit on Friday, which might accommodate some of you. Of course, the Chamber will also have to speak with the registry about it, also very practical matters like costs of cancelling, costs of adding sessions. We'll let you know as soon as possible, but I'd like to hear whether Thursday afternoon, apart from preparations, causes any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do believe I'll be starting first and I will be ready to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then at least we'll not make any further efforts to see whether we can have additional time on Friday. It might even that be that we can do without Friday. We adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, the 18th of December, at 9.00 in the morning in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of December, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
